baseline_models.focus_anchor: وَأَنذِرِ ٱلنَّاسَ يَوْمَ يَأْتِيهِمُ ٱلْعَذَابُ ... أَخِّرْنَآ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلٍۢ قَرِيبٍۢ
baseline_models.mechanism: Warning arouses caution before an arriving calamity, while the wrongdoers' first request after its arrival is for temporal deferral. The construction makes warning-time an actionable interval that closes when punishment-time arrives.

activation_trace.role: Warning communicates what is feared in order to awaken caution; it opens the pre-arrival action window.
The day can image a severe event that descends, not merely a calendar date; it marks the threshold.
Arrival gives the punishment directional completion and closes the distance presupposed by warning.
Deferral to a later time is the requested reversal of the completed arrival.
A fixed temporal limit makes the requested extension bounded rather than an escape from judgment.

changed_reading.before: The ayah announces a future punishment and reports a plea for more time.
changed_reading.after: The ayah stages a one-way temporal threshold: warning is usable before arrival, but after arrival the wrongdoers can only ask for the action-window to be reopened.

baseline_models.mechanism: The promised change has two linked motions: answer the summons and then travel in the messengers' wake. It is a proposed rerouting of responsiveness and allegiance, not an unspecified promise to behave better.

activation_trace.role: Answering supplies the verbal return that claims to meet the summons.
A call inclines its addressee by speech; it supplies the directive pole of the proposed realignment.
Following as going after another turns verbal response into sustained movement behind a guide.
The messengers and their carried message specify whose path the promised following would adopt.

changed_reading.before: They promise generic obedience if granted a short reprieve.
changed_reading.after: They promise to rewire a whole response sequence: receive the divine summons, return an answer, and continue behind its authorized carriers.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: أَوَلَمْ تَكُونُوٓا۟ أَقْسَمْتُم مِّن قَبْلُ مَا لَكُم مِّن زَوَالٍۢ
baseline_models.mechanism: The closing question confronts a former oath that excluded displacement or change. Its temporal priority and binding force make the present request for postponement the audible collapse of a previously secured self-image.

activation_trace.role: The oath is a formally binding assertion, increasing the force of its later contradiction.
Temporal precedence places confident denial before the present scene of compelled recognition.
Removal from place or state gives the denied change spatial, political, and existential breadth.

changed_reading.before: They had denied that they would die or disappear.
changed_reading.after: They had sworn themselves exempt from transfer out of their settled condition; the request for a new term is that oath collapsing under an actual change of state.

context_deltas.mechanism: Earlier, the messengers describe God as calling the addressees so that He may forgive them and defer them to a named term. The focus plea asks for deferral to a near term and promises to answer that call. The plea therefore requests a replay, in reversed order, of the offer previously refused.

activation_trace.role: The earlier divine call supplies the same summons that the focus speakers belatedly promise to answer.
Protective covering of the fault names the benefit attached to accepting the earlier call.
The earlier offer already contains postponement, making the focus request a demand for a missed provision.
The named limit fixes the earlier postponement within an assigned duration.
The focus answer is the response withheld when the call and postponement were available.

structural_cues: 14:10 sequences call, forgiveness, postponement, and fixed term; 14:44 sequences requested postponement, near term, and promised response.
The same roots for call, delay, and term recur on opposite sides of punishment's arrival.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the repeated lexical chain; I infer that reversed order marks a request to replay a refused offer. A live alternative is simple thematic repetition without deliberate reversal.

changed_reading.before: The plea invents a new bargain under pressure.
changed_reading.after: The plea asks to reactivate the exact call-and-delay arrangement once offered before judgment, but now promises response only after its term has closed.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah records a prior completed call-response pair: Satan called and they responded. Their focus promise to answer God's call is therefore not evidence that they lacked responsiveness; it is an attempted reassignment of a faculty already exercised toward the wrong caller.

activation_trace.role: Satan's call supplies the rival summons that actually inclined them in the earlier action-window.
Their completed response proves that answering was active but attached to the rival call.
Blame returns responsibility for that response to the responders rather than the caller.
The self as the person's own identity localizes liability for choosing which call to answer.
The divine call is now named as the object of a belatedly redirected response.

structural_cues: 14:22 has دَعَوْتُكُمْ فَٱسْتَجَبْتُمْ; 14:44 has نُّجِبْ دَعْوَتَكَ.
Both scenes occur in post-judgment speech where blame can no longer be transferred.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an exact rival call-response pair; I infer a contrast in allegiance rather than mere repetition of response vocabulary. Alternatively, 14:22 may establish culpability without being a direct foil to 14:44.

changed_reading.before: They failed to answer and now promise that they would.
changed_reading.after: They did answer a call in life; their plea promises a last-minute transfer of responsiveness from the caller they chose to the Caller they refused.

context_deltas.mechanism: The judgment scene identifies the weak as former followers of the arrogant, while Abraham's speech makes following a relation of belonging. The focus promise to follow the messengers is thus a proposed transfer of social attachment and identity after the old chain of leadership has failed.

activation_trace.role: Their prior position as people going behind human leaders supplies the failed allegiance being replaced.
Claimed greatness and pride characterize the leaders whose following yields no protection.
Following establishes affiliation with the followed, sharpening the identity at stake in the focus promise.
Messenger and carried message identify the authorized alternative to arrogant leadership.
The focus verb proposes entering the messengers' wake after the former following has broken down.

structural_cues: 14:21 explicitly says كُنَّا لَكُمْ تَبَعًا in the same judgment sequence.
14:44 changes only the object of following: from failed human superiors to the messengers.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies two objects of following and the affiliative use in 14:36; I infer a late transfer of allegiance. The alternative is that each occurrence independently denotes obedience without a social-chain contrast.

changed_reading.before: They promise to start obeying prophetic instructions.
changed_reading.after: They ask to defect from the collapsed follower-chain of the arrogant and enter the messengers' affiliative wake, but only after leadership can no longer be changed.

context_deltas.mechanism: Immediately before the focus, the audience is told not to mistake divine postponement for inattention: the wrongdoers are being delayed to a day of fixed gaze and emptied hearts. Their request 'delay us' occurs inside the day to which they had already been delayed, so it asks for a second postponement after the first has been fully spent.

activation_trace.role: Supposition supplies the mistaken reading that postponement means the account has been overlooked.
Inattention is explicitly denied, separating delay from forgotten liability.
Actual divine postponement supplies the already-consumed extension echoed by the focus imperative.
The fixed, raised gaze renders the terminal day as bodily incapacity rather than another deliberative interval.
The heart as empty space supplies the collapse from which the focus plea emerges.
Their imperative repeats the postponement root after its narrated extension has reached its endpoint.

structural_cues: 14:42 يُؤَخِّرُهُمْ لِيَوْمٍ is immediately answered by 14:44 أَخِّرْنَآ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلٍ.
The intervening body sequence moves from fixed eyes and raised heads to empty hearts before speech resumes.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the immediate root echo and terminal body sequence; I infer that the granted delay is exhausted rather than newly negotiable. A live alternative treats the two delays simply as divine action and human request without a spent-credit relation.

changed_reading.before: They ask for a short first extension once danger becomes visible.
changed_reading.after: They ask for another extension from inside the endpoint of an extension already granted, while the text denies that the earlier waiting ever meant neglect.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah defines the coming day as one without sale or permeating friendship, then as the standing of the account and the rapid settlement of every self. Against that procedural closure, 'a near term' sounds like an attempt to introduce credit or relational leverage into a phase where neither remains operative.

activation_trace.role: Exchange by price is absent on the coming day, removing transactional means of purchasing an extension.
Intimate attachment that permeates the self is also unavailable as relational leverage.
Counting and account define the day as settlement rather than a new performance period.
Speed excludes the slack that the requested near extension tries to recover.
The final account closes the procedural sequence in which the plea is made.
The requested fixed term functions like fresh temporal credit sought after settlement has begun.

structural_cues: 14:31 commands action before the day precisely because exchange and intimate leverage disappear there.
14:41 and 14:51 frame that day by the account, with 14:51 adding speed.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a no-exchange day, a standing account, and rapid settlement; I infer an economic-procedural analogy in the request for a new term. The alternative is a purely temporal plea without a credit metaphor.

changed_reading.before: They ask for a small amount of additional time.
changed_reading.after: They seek fresh temporal credit after the day has become a nonnegotiable settlement, when neither exchange nor relationship can reopen the account.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah repeatedly transfers habitation: opponents threaten expulsion, wrongdoers are destroyed, others are settled after them, and the current audience inhabits the former wrongdoers' dwellings after their fate has been made clear. The oath of 'no removal' is thus spoken from inside material evidence that occupants change while dwellings remain.

activation_trace.role: Expulsion supplies the contested movement out of a claimed land.
Destruction removes the wrongdoers who attempted to control that movement.
Resettlement after the removed people makes habitation explicitly transferable.
Living in predecessor dwellings turns settlement itself into evidence of earlier occupant removal.
Manifest disclosure makes that historical counterexample available rather than hidden.
The denied removal is contradicted by the transfer pattern encoded in the places they occupy.

structural_cues: 14:14 promises settlement after prior wrongdoers; 14:45 says the audience settled in those wrongdoers' dwellings.
14:45 follows the oath-question in 14:44, so the inhabited evidence answers the claim of permanence.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies successive removal and resettlement; I infer that continuity of buildings was misread as continuity of occupants. Alternatively, the dwelling notice may function only as historical admonition rather than a direct analysis of زوال.

changed_reading.before: Their oath asserts abstract personal permanence.
changed_reading.after: Their confidence mistakes stable-looking habitation for stable occupancy even while they live inside proof that wrongdoers are removed and their places reassigned.

context_deltas.mechanism: Immediately after the focus, removal is measured against mountains, and shortly afterward the earth itself is exchanged for another earth. The oath excluding any removal is therefore exposed at nested scales: person, regime, mountain, and world-order all stand inside possible displacement.

activation_trace.role: The immediate recurrence applies removal from place or state to mountains, enlarging the focus root's scale.
A high solid mass supplies the strongest visible benchmark for apparent immovability.
One thing standing in place of another turns cosmic stability into explicit substitution.
The lower world opposed to heaven is itself the object replaced, removing the presumed stable ground.
The oath's denial becomes untenable once the same removal image reaches mountains and earth.

structural_cues: The focus denial مَا لَكُم مِّن زَوَالٍ is followed two ayat later by لِتَزُولَ مِنْهُ ٱلْجِبَالُ.
14:48 then replaces the earth and heavens before universal emergence.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the immediate root echo and later earth-substitution; I infer a deliberate escalation of scale. The mountain clause may instead quantify the extremity or impotence of plotting, but either reading still destabilizes the oath's scale of permanence.

changed_reading.before: The oath denies only the speakers' death or departure.
changed_reading.after: The oath claims exemption from a displacement that the surah can apply even to mountains and the ground itself; personal permanence fails inside cosmic replaceability.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah gives speech a material ecology: a good word has a fixed root, while a corrupt word is pulled wholly from its root and has no settlement. The focus contains both a former oath of permanence and a new promise of response; context asks whether either utterance has roots in enacted following rather than merely asserting stability.

activation_trace.role: Meaningful speech connecting speakers supplies the verbal entity that receives a botanical structure.
A foundational root supplies the hidden support required for verbal stability.
Durable fixation defines stability as supported persistence rather than verbal insistence.
Whole-root extraction supplies the failure mode of speech lacking a viable foundation.
The absence of fixed settlement names what the corrupt verbal tree cannot secure.
The former oath is a forceful utterance whose claimed permanence can now be tested for rooted support.

structural_cues: 14:24-27 repeatedly binds word, root, fixation, uprooting, settlement, and saying.
14:44 juxtaposes a newly spoken promise with an earlier sworn permanence that events have uprooted.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the word-tree mechanism and two focus utterances; I infer that the mechanism audits the utterances' enacted roots. A live alternative confines the word-tree comparison to its immediate unit and does not project it onto this plea.

changed_reading.before: The earlier oath was simply false and the new promise may be sincere.
changed_reading.after: Both are verbal attempts to claim stability; the surah's word-tree test shifts attention from intensity of speech to whether response and following ever rooted it in action.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah opens with a public movement out of darkness into light and closes by naming itself a delivered communication for people to be warned, know, and remember. The focus imperative is therefore not isolated threat-display; it is the final public exit mechanism offered before arrival.

activation_trace.role: Passage to the outside gives the message an intended movement away from enclosure.
Illumination supplies the destination in which danger and route become visible.
Delivery of a message frames the surah as communication that reaches its public.
The closing warning repeats the focus function of awakening caution through feared consequence.
Knowledge as disclosure names the cognitive change warning is meant to produce.
Bringing something back into active awareness completes warning's intended uptake.
The focus command occupies the surah-wide communication pathway from disclosure to caution.

structural_cues: The مخاطب الناس of 14:44 is enclosed by الناس in the opening exit-program and closing proclamation.
The closing sequence links delivery, warning, knowledge, and remembrance as successive uptake functions.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies opening movement and closing communication functions; I infer that warning is an offered exit rather than spectacle alone. The alternative is that opening and closing are broad framing devices without a specific mechanism for 14:44.

changed_reading.before: The command asks the messenger to frighten people with a future scene.
changed_reading.after: The warning is the surah's last public route from enclosure to disclosed knowledge and remembered caution before the arriving day makes voluntary exit impossible.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates the sweet-water and abstention branches of ع ذ ب rather than replacing the ordinary punishment branch. It remains anchored in the focus noun and in 14:16-17's explicit administered water that cannot be swallowed. Downstream prose should present it only as a sensory counter-image within this surah, not as an etymological redefinition of punishment.

activation_trace.role: Potable sweetness supplies the positive water-pole that the punishment scene materially reverses.
Abstention from food or drink supplies the bodily non-intake realized when liquid cannot become drink.
Giving drink supplies the forced watering action.
Water itself supplies the expected medium of refreshment.
Smooth passage through the throat is nearly impossible, converting water into blocked intake.
Painful punishment names the dominant sense while the water branches supply its sensory inversion.

changed_reading.before: Punishment is an abstract penalty that arrives.
changed_reading.after: Within this surah's material staging, punishment also feels like anti-watering: liquid is administered yet denied the smooth, life-serving passage expected of drink.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is a cross-domain juridical reading assembled from focus branches for withheld right, claim, liability, oath, and fixed term, then sharpened by the final account. It remains anchored in several focus constructions, but the ayah does not explicitly call itself a court proceeding. Downstream prose should mark it as a legal-mechanism analogy, not a syntactic determination.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا۟ ... أَجَلٍۢ ... دَعْوَتَكَ وَنَتَّبِعِ ... أَقْسَمْتُم

activation_trace.role: Withholding or confining a right casts wrongdoing as an unresolved liability.
A fixed term supplies the deadline after which the liability matures.
Assertion of a right supplies a summons-like edge to the call they promise to answer.
An attached consequence or liability makes following carry what trails an earlier act.
The oath supplies a prior binding representation now contradicted by the speakers' position.
Exacting and settling a debt supplies the terminal collection mechanism.
The account gathers the acts into a closed reckoning.

changed_reading.before: The wrongdoers make an emotional appeal for another chance.
changed_reading.after: The plea can be carried as an attempt to reopen a closed case after its fixed term: answer the summons now, assume the proper liability now, despite the prior oath and matured account.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it uses the packet's non-dominant ق ل ل mapping for focus ق و ل, especially its shudder and instability branches. It remains formally anchored to يَقُولُ and gains contextual support from fixed sight and emptied hearts immediately before the speech. Downstream prose must label it a consonantal branch activation, not the lexical meaning of يقول.

activation_trace.role: Shudder and agitation recast the utterance as a bodily symptom of fear.
Instability and movement make the speech itself register the collapse of their non-removal claim.
A fixed, protruding gaze supplies the body's arrested visual state before speech.
Interior emptiness supplies the affective void from which the plea breaks out.
Movement and agitation after stillness invert the speakers' former denial of any destabilization.

changed_reading.before: Their plea is a composed verbal proposal.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the saying is also the first tremor of the permanence they had asserted: fixed eyes, emptied hearts, and destabilized speech expose the oath bodily.

strongest_changes: 14:10 makes the plea a reversed replay of an earlier call, forgiveness, postponement, and fixed term that had been refused.
14:22 shows that they did answer a call, but the wrong one; 14:21 likewise shows that they followed, but the wrong leaders.
14:42 makes their requested delay a second extension sought from inside the endpoint of delay already granted.
14:45-48 answer the oath of no removal with transferred dwellings, potentially moving mountains, and a replaced earth.
summary.what_was_special: Whole-surah context turns nearly every promise in 14:44 into a reversal of an earlier exercised choice: call was refused, response and following were misdirected, delay was spent, and permanence was asserted while predecessor dwellings and the created order displayed replaceability.
remaining_uncertainties: The mountain-removal clause can scale either the force or the impotence of plotting, though both readings destabilize claimed permanence.
Applying the rooted-word mechanism of 14:24-27 directly to the oath and plea in 14:44 is coherent but not explicit.
The anti-watering, closed-case, and speech-tremor models depend on branch-distant or cross-domain activation and should remain exploratory.
